Word frequencies in the comments

Source: R/comments.R
delphi_words.Rd

Counts the words used in the comments, after removing common words (articles, prepositions, pronouns and auxiliary verbs) in English and Italian. Word frequencies give a first, descriptive view of the content of the comments; they do not replace a qualitative reading of the comments.

Usage

delphi_words(
  x,
  round = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  language = c("en", "it"),
  stopwords = NULL,
  min_length = 3,
  top = 20
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object with comments; see delphi_add_comments().

round, items

Optional subsets of rounds and items.

language

Languages whose common words are removed: any of "en" (English) and "it" (Italian), or NULL to keep all words.

stopwords

Additional words to remove, for example the words used in every item statement.

min_length

Minimum number of letters of the words to count.

top

Number of words to return; NULL returns all of them.

Value

A data frame with columns word, n (number of occurrences) and n_comments (number of comments in which the word appears), ordered by decreasing frequency.

Details

Comments are converted to lower case and split into words at every character that is not a letter, so that numbers and punctuation are discarded and elided forms such as dell'impatto are split into two words. No stemming is applied: "policy" and "policies" are counted as different words.

Examples

r1 <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "B", "C"), E1 = c(7, 8, 6))
x <- delphi_data(r1, expert_col = "expert", indicator = "impact")
cm <- data.frame(expert = c("A", "B", "C"), item = "E1",
                 comment = c("Public funding is essential.",
                             "Without public funding, no impact.",
                             "Regulation matters more than funding."))
x <- delphi_add_comments(x, cm)
delphi_words(x)
#>         word n n_comments
#> 1    funding 3          3
#> 2     public 2          2
#> 3  essential 1          1
#> 4     impact 1          1
#> 5    matters 1          1
#> 6 regulation 1          1
